title: Electronics I: Analog Circuits
full_title: Electronics I: Diodes, MOSFETs, BJT, and Amplifier Design
summary: Electronics turns devices into useful circuits. This course models diodes and transistors for circuit design, biases MOSFET and BJT amplifiers, analyses single- and multistage amplifiers with small-signal models, and introduces current mirrors, differential pairs and the frequency response of amplifiers.
overview: Analog electronics is the one that the diode and the transistor and the amplifier is for, of the signal, and the one that the limit is for. From the diode and the rectifier, through the bias and the small signal, to the amplifier and the frequency, and the one that the design is for.

The diode and the rectifier. The bias and the small signal. The amplifier and the frequency. The design and the limit. This course is the one that the analog is for, of the design, and the one that the limit is for.
outcomes: Use the diode and the rectifier, together, for a power stage.
Use the bias and the small signal, together, for a transistor stage.
Use the amplifier and the frequency, together, for a system.
Use the current mirror and the differential, together, for a design.

chapters.title: Diode circuits
chapters.summary: Diode models, rectifiers, peak detectors, clippers, clampers and Zener regulators.

chapters.title: MOSFET circuits and biasing
chapters.summary: Large-signal MOSFET models, DC analysis and biasing networks, and the MOSFET as a switch and as an amplifier.

chapters.title: BJT circuits and biasing
chapters.summary: Large-signal BJT models, DC analysis, bias stability, and the BJT as a switch and as an amplifier.

chapters.title: Small-signal models and amplifier basics
chapters.summary: Small-signal equivalent circuits, voltage gain, input and output resistance, and amplifier models.

chapters.title: Single-stage amplifiers
chapters.summary: Common-source and common-emitter, common-gate and common-base, and source- and emitter-follower amplifiers.

chapters.title: Multistage amplifiers
chapters.summary: Cascading stages, the cascode, Darlington pairs and the design of amplifier chains.

chapters.title: Current sources and mirrors
chapters.summary: Current mirrors and improved mirrors, current sources as active loads, and biasing in integrated circuits.

chapters.title: Differential amplifiers
chapters.summary: The differential pair, differential and common-mode gain, common-mode rejection, active loads and mismatch.

chapters.title: Frequency response of amplifiers
chapters.summary: Low- and high-frequency transistor models, the Miller effect, open-circuit time constants and amplifier bandwidth.
